pandas.DataFrame.insert

pandas 3.1.1 · DataFrame · method

Insert a column at the specified position in the existing DataFrame. A column with the same name raises ValueError by default.

  • Call syntax
  • Run the example
  • Parameters
  • Returns

Call syntax

DataFrame.insert(loc, column, value, allow_duplicates=False)

Run the example

Edit the example and select Run Python to see the result.


    

    
Parameters
ParameterRequirementAccepted values and behavior
loc
      Required
Positional or keyword		
      int
The zero-based position for the new column. Use 0 for the first column. Use the number of existing columns to append.


column
      Required
Positional or keyword		
      str, number, or hashable object
The name of the new column. Use a string, a number, or another hashable label.


value
      Required
Positional or keyword		
      Scalar, Series, or array-like
Data for the new column. A scalar is repeated in every row. An array or list must match the row count. A Series aligns by the DataFrame index, leaving missing values for unmatched rows.


allow_duplicates
      Optional
Positional or keyword
Default False		
      bool
The default False raises ValueError if the name already exists. Set True to allow the duplicate when the DataFrame permits duplicate labels.

    
Returns
Returns None and adds the column to the existing DataFrame.
